extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the Singular computer algebra system (mathematicians/programmers writing Singular scripts and libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for Singular's user-defined types, pyobject (Python interop), reference/shared experimental types, and many built-in kernel functions; explains syntax, semantics, restrictions and examples for correct usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments for user defined types
rubrics_metrics.description: By default, only objects of the same (user defined) type can be assigned; there is no automatic type conversion as for the kernel data types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can override the operator = to write custom constructors via system("install", user type ,"=", p, 1); the user type must be given as a string. The custom constructor does not apply to assignments of the same type. The user defined procedure for = also provides generic type conversions: e.g. hh A=hh(b); is equivalent to creating a tmp, assigning, then killing tmp. Examples show newstruct and system("install",...,"=",...).

rubrics_metrics.name: cone (convex rational polyhedral cone) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: A cone is the convex set generated by finitely many half-lines (rational/integer points); it may contain a lineality space and can be represented either by rays (generators) or by homogeneous integer linear inequalities/equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singular uses gfanlib for convex objects — check readme/install instructions. Cones in Singular can be created via the gfan interface (see coneViaPoints and coneViaInequalities). Example: LIB"gfan.lib"; cone c; cone c = 17; (see gfan lib section).

rubrics_metrics.name: fan (polyhedral fan) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: A polyhedral fan is a collection of cones closed under intersections and faces; Singular exposes constructors like emptyFan(n), fullFan(n), and accepts an optional symmetry group intmat G whose rows generate a subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singular will check validity of provided G rows as permutations. Use LIB("gfan.lib"). Examples and convenience overloads documented (emptyFan with optional G behaves like emptyFan(n)). See gfan lib section for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: polytope representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational convex polytope in R^n is represented internally as a cone in R^(n+1) intersected with the hyperplane where the first coordinate equals 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To use polytopes use gfanlib (LIB("gfan.lib")). See D.13.1 for the interface and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: pyobject availability / loading
rubrics_metrics.description: pyobject is a black box data type for handling Python objects; this feature is automatically loaded on demand when initializing a pyobject, but you can explicitly load its support with LIB("pyobject.so");
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need pyobject-related functions before creating a python object, explicitly LIB("pyobject.so"); examples show python_eval, python_run, python_import behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: pyobject declaration syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: pyobject name = pyobject expression ; — defines a python object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: pyobject empty; pyobject pystr = "Hello World!"; pyobject pyone = 17; pyobject pylst = list(pystr, pyone); printing examples show returned pyobjects like [ 'Hello World!', 17 ].

rubrics_metrics.name: pyobject expression composition rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A pyobject expression may be: 1) an identifier of type pyobject; 2) a function returning pyobject; 3) pyobject expressions combined by +, -, *, /, ^; 4) a list expression whose elements are pyobject expressions; 5) a string expression; 6) an int expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate combining pystrings, pyints, lists, and using python_eval/range to create lists. See Section 3.5.5 references for type conversion/casting.

rubrics_metrics.name: pyobject operations and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Supported operators: +, -, *, / (add/sub/mul/div), ^/** (power by positive integer), comparators (<, <=, >, >=, ==, <>), indexing [int], call (pyobject expression ( ... )), attribute access . and :: (string or name).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations follow Python semantics insofar as types permit: concatenating str + int errors (cannot concatenate 'str' and 'int'), but str * int repeats string. Comparators consider leading monomials w.r.t monomial ordering. Examples show arithmetic and comparison results. Some operations may produce errors when types mismatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: attrib / killattrib for pyobjects and general attrib usage
rubrics_metrics.description: attrib(name) displays attribute list of object; attrib(name, string) returns the value of that attribute (empty string if not defined); attrib(name, string, expression) sets the attribute to expression. killattrib deletes an attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserved attributes exist and some are used by the kernel (see reserved list in attrib general section). Examples: attrib(pystr, "count") or attrib(func, "func_name", "byAnyOtherName"); killattrib demonstrated on a dynamically created attribute. See Section 5.1.2 and 5.1.70.

rubrics_metrics.name: python_run / python_eval / python_import behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: python_run(string) executes Python commands and syncs contexts afterwards (no return), python_eval(string) evaluates a Python expression and returns a pyobject, python_import(string) imports a Python module into Singular context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: python_run("def newfunc(*args): return list(args)"); newfunc becomes known to Singular. python_eval("17+4") returns pyobject 21. python_import("os") makes os, name, sep, linesep available. Use LIB("pyobject.so") first if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: python attribute access convenience notations
rubrics_metrics.description: You can access Python attributes via attrib(obj, "attr"), or via short notations obj."attr"() or obj.attr() when the attribute name is valid and unused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: proc(attrib(pylst, "sort"))(); pylst.sort(); pylst."sort"(); and pystr.count("a") demonstrates shorter access forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: reference/shared experimental feature activation
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference and shared types are experimental and hidden by default — enable with system("reference"); or system("shared");
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activation is required before declaring reference/shared objects. Documentation warns features are experimental and examples show behavior after activation.

rubrics_metrics.name: reference semantics and initialization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference stores a handle to an existing (named) identifier or a subexpression thereof; copying a reference only adds another handle to the same object instance. You must initialize a reference using a named identifier or a subexpression of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: reference ref = i; ref = 19 updates i as well. Uninitialized references print '<unassigned reference or shared memory>' and cannot be assigned from non-named expressions (error message shown). Use reference to implement side-effecting procedures. See reference declarations and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: shared semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: shared is like reference but can be initialized from an expression (does not require initial identifier); copies have equal rights to manipulate the shared data; all operations of the underlying objects are forwarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: shared ll = list(2,3); modifying ll[1] changes value in place. shared prints '_' for uninitialized shared. Use system("shared") to enable. Shared is useful to avoid duplicating data and for concurrency-like shared access.

rubrics_metrics.name: type-change restriction for references
rubrics_metrics.description: References cannot change the referenced object's type by assignment — assigning a differently-typed value to a reference yields a type error (e.g., 'string' = 'int' is not supported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates error when assigning integer to a reference of a string; assign via correct typed values or reconstruct the referenced object if type change is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: reference and shared declaration syntaxes
rubrics_metrics.description: reference name = identifier ; shared name = expression ; — define reference and shared objects respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: reference ref = str; shared sh = 17; shared empty; reference empty; shows behavior and printed forms ('<unassigned reference or shared memory>' or '_' for shared).

rubrics_metrics.name: reference/shared expression categories
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference expression can be any identifier, any subexpression of an identifier, or an object of type reference; a shared expression can be any expression or an object of type shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show reference lref = ll[1] ties to the list element; shared lref = ll[1] ties similarly. The documentation explains how expressions of these types reference original data.

rubrics_metrics.name: dereferencing rules and when explicit dereference needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Most operations on reference/shared objects are automatically dereferenced; however, explicit dereferencing is needed in some contexts (e.g., n-ary function calls not starting with a reference/shared object, or constructs that prematurely evaluate left-hand subexpressions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workarounds: use link(ref) to explicitly dereference, use poly(xsh) type cast, or def operator to disambiguate. Examples: subst(p, poly(xsh),1, y,2, z,3) or subst(p, link(xsh),1, y,2, z,3) succeed while subst(p, xsh,1,...) fails. Also def(ll[1]) = 11 replaces all tied entries in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: def and link functions for reference/shared
rubrics_metrics.description: def explicitly type-casts to reference or shared; link explicitly dereferences a reference/shared object (extracts the underlying object).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: def(ll[2]) = x; link(shl); list(shl) vs link(shl) show difference between wrapping and extracting. Use def to avoid premature evaluation or to force reference semantics in calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: system overload for reference/shared
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference and shared objects overload the system command to provide extended features; use system(ref, "help") to see available operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: system(<ref>, count), system(<ref>, enumerate), system(<ref>, undefined), system(<ref>, "typeof"), system(<ref1>, same, <ref2>) - tests for identical reference objects. Listings show number of references pointing to <ref>, unique id, assigned check, and actual referenced type.

rubrics_metrics.name: attrib (general kernel function) usage and reserved attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: attrib(name) displays attribute list; attrib(name, string) returns attribute value or empty string if undefined; attrib(name, string, expression) sets attribute. Kernel uses several reserved attributes (cf_class, global, isSB, isHomog, isCI, isCM, maxExp, rank, ring_cf, withSB, withHilb, withRes, withDim, withMult).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserved attributes are used by the kernel and libraries; non-reserved attributes can be user-defined and may speed up computations. Examples show attrib on ideals and maxideal to inspect 'isSB'. See killattrib for deletion and refer to library sections for attribute-specific semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: bareiss function behavior and return values
rubrics_metrics.description: bareiss(module or matrix[, int i, int j]) applies the sparse Gauss–Bareiss algorithm to a module/matrix; with one parameter it performs complete elimination and returns a list whose first entry is a module with a minimal independent set of vectors (matrix lower triangular) and second entry is an intvec with the permutation of rows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameters bareiss(M,i,j) control skipping diagonalization of the last i rows and stop reduction when remaining vectors ≤ j. Examples illustrate full elimination and partial eliminations; see det and matrix sections for related behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: betti function purpose and caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: betti(resolution or list [, int minimizeFlag]) computes graded Betti numbers of a minimal resolution of R^n/M using the provided resolution; result is an intmat with counts of minimal generators by degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: betti uses only initial monomials — this can give confusing results for non-homogeneous input. If the optional second argument is non-zero, Betti numbers are minimized. betti sets attribute rowShift. Examples show interpreting printed Betti matrix and mapping to syzygy modules and degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: char function
rubrics_metrics.description: char(ring name) returns the characteristic of the coefficient field of a ring (int).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: char(r) → 32003 for ring r=32003,(x,y),dp; char returns 0 for characteristic zero fields (e.g., QQ or real). See charstr for string description.

rubrics_metrics.name: char_series function
rubrics_metrics.description: char_series(ideal) returns a matrix whose rows represent the irreducible characteristic series of the ideal with respect to current variable ordering; useful for decomposing zero-sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: char_series(ideal(xyz,xz,y)) prints rows that correspond to components like 'y,z' and 'x,y'. Cross-reference: Characteristic sets section.

rubrics_metrics.name: charstr function
rubrics_metrics.description: charstr(ring name) returns a string description of the coefficient field of a ring (e.g., 'ZZ/32003', 'QQ', '7,a', 'Float()').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: String representation may change; tests and routines should use ring.lib routines as charstr can vary. Examples show different ring definitions and their charstr outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: chinrem function constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: chinrem(list, intvec) or chinrem(list, list) / chinrem(intvec,intvec) applies the Chinese remainder theorem to the first argument w.r.t. the moduli given in the second; the elements of the first list must be of the same type (bigint/int, poly, ideal, module or matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data depending on a ring are involved, the coefficient field must be Q. Examples demonstrate using chinrem on integers, ideals, and nested lists. Moduli may be intvec or list of bigints.

rubrics_metrics.name: cleardenom function
rubrics_metrics.description: cleardenom(poly or vector) multiplies a polynomial/vector by a suitable constant to cancel all denominators in coefficients and then divides by its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cleardenom((3x+6y)^5 / 5) yields integer-polynomial content-cancelled form; applied to vectors clears denominators elementwise and divides by gcd content. See content function library for related operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: close (link) function
rubrics_metrics.description: close(link) closes a previously opened link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: opening a server link via open(l) and then close(l) shuts down the Singular server. See link/open sections for link syntax and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: coef function behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: coef(f, m) determines the monomials in f divisible by ring-variable product m and returns a 2×n matrix: first row monomials, second row corresponding coefficients as polynomials in remaining variables (f = sum M[1,i]*M[2,i]). In the vector/matrix variant, two matrix arguments are used to receive coefficients and monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coef to factor out specified variable monomials and inspect coefficients. See examples and notes about types and matrix-return variants.
